label: Place
name: Mumbai
summary:
Mumbai, also known as Bombay, is the capital of Maharashtra state and the financial capital and most populous city of India, with 12.5 million in the city and 21 million in the metropolitan area. Located on a peninsula on the west coast of India, Mumbai handles over 60% of India's trade and generates approximately 6% of national GDP — a concentration of economic power unmatched by any other Indian city.

The site was originally a cluster of seven islands inhabited by Koli fisherfolk. The islands passed through Portuguese control (ceded 1534), British possession (transferred as part of Catherine of Braganza's dowry to Charles II in 1661), and East India Company administration before becoming the busiest port in Asia. The cotton trade, opium export to China, and the opening of the Suez Canal (1869) transformed Bombay into a major Victorian commercial metropolis. The Great Indian Peninsular Railway linked it to Calcutta and Delhi; by 1900 it was the largest city in Asia after Tokyo.

Mumbai's 20th century was defined by the textile mill industry (employing 250,000 workers at its peak), independence from Britain (1947), the Maharashtra-Gujarat linguistic partition (1960), and the rise of Bollywood — the world's largest film industry by ticket sales. The 1992–93 communal riots following the Babri Masjid demolition and the 2008 Mumbai attacks (killing 166 people) are defining traumas. With its financial district Bandra-Kurla Complex, stock exchange (BSE), and the Reserve Bank of India, Mumbai anchors the entire South Asian financial system.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Mumbai's emergence as a major port and economic hub facilitated India's integration into global trade networks, contributing to the country's rapid industrialization and modernization in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

causes: British East India Company development of the natural harbor (1668 onward) transforming the seven islands into a major trading port
Opening of the Suez Canal (1869) dramatically shortening the Europe-India trade route and making Mumbai India's premier port
Railway connection to the Indian interior (1853) enabling Mumbai to serve as the commercial gateway for all of western India
Cotton industry boom (19th century) and Bollywood's emergence (20th century) creating the dual economic foundation
effects: Most important financial center in South Asia — hosting BSE, NSE, Reserve Bank of India, and all major Indian banks
Bollywood — world's largest film industry by ticket sales, producing over 1,000 films per year
Mumbai 2008 attacks — coordinated terrorist assault killing 166 people that transformed Indian security policy
Dharavi — one of Asia's largest informal settlements (1 million people in 2.1 km²) representing the extreme urban inequality of India's growth

relationships.context: Mumbai is situated within the Age of Exploration (941)
Mumbai shaped regional development during the Early Modern era
